title: After fixing strict 6-month order cutoffs, how accurately does Med Agent Hub read HIV charts on a shared cloud GPU?
summary: We tested whether tightening Med Agent Hub's date-window filters fixes a stubborn failure mode: mixing older lab or imaging orders into a strict 6-month lookback, or dropping earlier drug refills inside that same window. Both setups — OpenMRS's built-in ChartSearchAI and Med Agent Hub's single-call answer path — ran the exact same Google Gemma 4 12B model on a shared 24 GB cloud GPU across three HIV patients and 17 clinical scenarios (35 questions per setup, 70 answers total), anchored to June 20, 2026 and graded blind by two independent AI judges.
takeaway: Med Agent Hub scored 89.8/100 (9.32/10 accuracy, 9.03/10 completeness, 9.12/10 clarity) versus 75.4/100 for built-in ChartSearchAI — a +14.4-point lead with zero unsafe answers, zero wrong dates (vs. 3 on built-in), zero unnecessary refusals (vs. 4 on built-in), and 100% verified chart citations (94/94). On the 6-month orders question that motivated this test, Med Agent Hub jumped from 53.0 to 94.0/100 by capturing all eight qualifying prescriptions across both January and December visits while excluding December 14 labs and chest X-rays that fell six days outside the cutoff. Trade-off and remaining gap: Med Agent Hub averaged 17.0s per answer vs. 4.4s on built-in ChartSearchAI, and its one weak spot (53.0/100) was a 5-turn counseling follow-up about stopping an older HIV medication.
